prompt: Let $f(x) = x^3 - x - 1$, which is continuous everywhere. You compute $f(1) = -1$, $f(1.5) = 0.875$ and $f(2) = 5$. Which interval MUST contain a zero of $f$, according to the Intermediate Value Theorem?

choices.label: None of these can be guaranteed.

hint: The IVT guarantees a zero on an interval whenever the function is continuous and changes SIGN across it.

hints.text: The IVT guarantees a zero on an interval whenever the function is continuous and changes SIGN across it.
Look at the signs: $f(1) < 0$, $f(1.5) > 0$, $f(2) > 0$. Where does the sign flip?
Negative at $1$, positive at $1.5$ — the sign flips on $[1, 1.5]$, so a zero is guaranteed there.

explanation: On $[1, 1.5]$: $f(1) = -1 < 0$ and $f(1.5) = 0.875 > 0$. Zero lies between those outputs, so the IVT gives a $c$ with $f(c) = 0$.
On $[1.5, 2]$ both values are positive, so the IVT promises nothing there.
On $[0, 1]$: $f(0) = -1$ and $f(1) = -1$, both negative — again no guarantee. Only A is forced.

alternativeExplanations.title: This is the bisection method
steps: Start with $[1, 2]$, where the sign changes. Check the midpoint $1.5$: positive.
Keep the half where the sign still changes: $[1, 1.5]$.
Repeat with midpoint $1.25$ ($f(1.25) \approx -0.297$, negative), so the zero is in $[1.25, 1.5]$ — the real root is about $1.3247$.
